title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Meridian Insurance
summary: Initial POC scoping to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Customer seeks low latency (p95 <200ms), predictable cost, and strict data residency. Discussed workload sizing, benchmark plan (latency/cost/regression), expected timeline (~6-8 weeks), and required security artifacts.
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood. Samir from our SE team is here, we'll run through the POC goals and then dig into your workload.
00:10 Marta (Meridian): Hi all, thanks. We got a short agenda - success criteria, sizing, security constraints, and timeline. We're trying to decide if hosted is ok or we need dedicated or private.
00:22 Samir (Redwood): Great. Quick intro - hosted is our managed API, fastest to start; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; private gives VPC or on-prem with customer control.
00:35 Lee (Meridian): Right, important thing: we can't send PII off-shore. Data residency + SOC2 are musts. We might need KMS integration and audit logs.
00:45 Noah (Meridian): Also our peak is during claims intake - about 250 concurrent agents, average request 350 tokens, bursts to 600 qps for short windows.
00:58 Samir (Redwood): Ok that helps. To ballpark, 250 concurrent with 350 tokens/request - we generally size for throughput and latency tradeoff. For hosted, we can route to low-latency regions but cost is usage-based; dedicated gives you reserved capacity to keep p95 low and predictable. Private would be best for strict residency and on-prem regulation.
01:20 Marta: Our success criteria - 1) Latency p95 <200ms for single-turn generation in critical path; 2) Cost target less than $X per 1k tokens (we left X placeholder, want your pricing); 3) Data never leaves our VPC for some workloads; 4) Clear audit logs and SSO.
01:36 Alex: Good explicit goals. On the latency number, depends on model size. If you're okay with a smaller open model we can hit <200ms p95 on A100 pools; for larger models it's tougher. We also have batching and cache to reduce cost.
01:50 Lee: Could you clarify caching - prefix caching? KV cache?
01:55 Samir: Yeah, we have prefix/KV cache and session affinity. If many requests share context (like policy templates) KV caching reduces repeated compute. But that helps only if requests have similar prefixes.
02:10 Noah: For our pipeline many calls are short prompts with template + claim text. So caching could help.
02:18 Marta: How do we compare hosted vs dedicated on security? Hosted meets SOC2 and region controls, but we need SSO and KMS - are those available on hosted?
02:28 Alex: Hosted supports SSO/SAML and we've integrations with customer-managed KMS for some enterprise tiers; Dedicated and Private offer stronger isolation and optional customer KMS. We'll share the specific security datasheet.
02:40 Lee: Great. For benchmark plan, what do you propose?
02:44 Samir: We usually run three benchmarks: latency under our p95 SLO with realistic payloads, throughput/cost to estimate unit economics, and quality/regression tests against a small eval set. Step-by-step: 1) you share sample prompts + dataset; 2) we run hosted baseline to get numbers; 3) if needed we spin a dedicated pilot with identical workload and compare; 4) if residency compliance requires, we set up private trial.
03:10 Marta: Timeline? We need results for Q2 planning. Ideally a decision in 6-8 weeks.
03:16 Alex: That's doable. Typical timeline: week 0-1 kickoff + dataset + security paperwork; week 2 hosted benchmark + initial results; week 3-4 dedicated pilot (if requested) and tuning; week 5 quality eval & cost analysis; week 6 decision and next steps. If Private is required, plan extends depending on VPC/provisioning - add 2-4 weeks for network setup.
03:38 Noah: About cost - we need an estimate for tokens/sec cost and monthly committed for dedicated.
03:44 Samir: We'll send a pricing sheet. As a rough example, for a 13B open model on A100, hosted cost might be $0.02 per 1k tokens (example only), dedicated reserved nodes might drop your unit cost by 30-40% depending on commit. We'll provide modeled scenarios based on your concurrency numbers.
04:02 Lee: Any hard limits on burst capacity? We need headroom for spikes without dropping requests.
04:07 Alex: Dedicated has burst options and autoscaling policies; hosted has rate limiting by quotas but can be configured for higher throughput. For very spiky latency-sensitive traffic you can set a fallback policy to a smaller model or route to another region. We can configure graceful degradation.
04:26 Marta: On security docs - we need SOC2 type II report, network diagrams, audit log samples, and KMS integration docs.
04:34 Alex: We'll share the security pack and a pointer to the compliance portal.
04:38 Noah: For dedicated pilot, what access do our ops engineers need?
04:42 Samir: Typically access to our console for observability; for Dedicated we provide a tenant with RBAC, and for Private we work with your infra to set up VPC peering/IP allowlists. You'll need a point of contact for network and key management.
04:59 Lee: Ok. A few technical clarifications: 1) quantization support (8-bit/4-bit) for cost savings; 2) kernel selection and performance for long sequences; 3) support for streaming responses and function/tool calling.
05:14 Samir: We support quantization-friendly execution, continuous KV cache, attention optimizations, and streaming. We'll include model-compatibility notes. Note sometimes names get munged in transcrip - our "Redwood Private" sometimes appears as "Redwood Privat" in notes :)
05:30 Marta: (laughs) noted.
05:33 Alex: Any known competitors we should watch out for? Marta: We're evaluating Anthropic and Vertex AI for managed endpoints; also some teams prototype with OpenAI but need better residency.
05:46 Alex: Understood. We'll highlight differences: latency predictability and isolation are primary value props for dedicated/private.
05:51 Noah: Ok, let's talk about concrete success criteria again so we can sign off the POC.
05:55 Marta: 1) p95 latency <200ms for critical route; 2) quality equal or better than our current baseline (we'll share eval prompts); 3) cost projection that meets finance constraints; 4) security artifacts provided; 5) a clear handoff plan to dedicated/private if selected.
06:12 Samir: We'll run targeted latency tests on your prompts against two model families - a lower-latency 7-13B family and a higher-quality 70B variant. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, and cost per 1k tokens.
06:28 Lee: For the dedicated pilot, what does the onboarding look like? Provisioning time?
06:32 Alex: Provisioning for Dedicated reserved pool typically 5-7 business days once contract and network info are finalized. Private VPC deployments can be 2-4 weeks depending on procurement and firewall change windows.
06:45 Marta: Who will run the benchmarks on your side vs ours?
06:49 Samir: We can run the hosted baseline ourselves if you provide dataset and a service account. For dedicated, we prefer a joint run - our SE will run tests while your ops monitors. We'll also give you the scripts and synthetic load tools.
07:05 Noah: On dataset - we'll sanitize and share ~500 sample prompts and an eval suite of ~150 labelled cases. Timing: we'll aim to deliver that by Friday.
07:12 Alex: Perfect. We'll schedule the hosted run for the following week.
07:16 Marta: For acceptance criteria, who signs off? Product + Security + Finance?
07:20 Lee: Product and Security for technical acceptance, Finance for cost approval. We'll loop in procurement for contract.
07:27 Alex: Great. Any other questions?
07:30 Marta: Not right now. Thanks, this was helpful.
07:33 Alex: Ok recap and next steps...
07:35 Alex: Recap: 1) Meridian to send sample prompts and eval set by Friday; 2) Redwood to run hosted baseline and share results + price scenarios; 3) If needed, spin dedicated pilot week 3-4; 4) Redwood to share security pack and SOC2.
07:50 Marta: Sounds good.
07:52 Lee: Thanks everyone.
07:54 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and send the docs. Bye.
07:58 Meeting end.
